newsitem.title: India: Mother Teresa recovering after taking oxygen.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa recovering after taking oxygen.

text.p: Doctors said Mother Teresa was recovering slowly on Tuesday after being given oxygen overnight to overcome a brief spell of breathing trouble.
"Mother Teresa is stabilising slowly," Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in an update on the condition of the 86-year-old nun, recovering from heart surgery and pneumonia.
Earlier on Tuesday, the hospital said the Roman Catholic missionary had a breathing problem at around 2.30 a.m. (2100 GMT Monday).
"It lasted for a few minutes and she was put on an oxygen mask," the medical bulletin said. "She is all right now. She had her morning tea around 7.45 a.m. and her prayer."
Last month, Mother Teresa, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, had surgery to unblock two coronary arteries, the third such operation in five years.
Her recovery has been complicated by her irregular heartbeat as well as lung and kidney problems.
On Monday, doctors gave her a second mild electric shock in six days to correct her faltering heartbeat. They said the procedure, called cardioversion, was a success.
"Her cardiac status is recovering after cardioversion yesterday," the hospital said.
But bronchitis, which has dogged Mother Teresa since her youth, continued to worry the doctors.
"Her pulmonary status shows minor improvement requiring continuous respiratory therapy. Pneumonia seems to be clearing but some bronchitis persists," the doctors said.

Hospital staff are helping the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner do simple deep breathing exercises to help relax her throat and chest muscles and keep fluid from collecting in her lungs, the doctors said.
Apart from massaging her chest every five or six hours to remove fluid, doctors are making her breathe deeply as she sits up and lies down.

Mother Teresa, who has been asking doctors to let her go home, called her Missionaries of Charity religious order on Monday evening and playfully asked the sisters there to send an ambulance to pick her up, doctors said.
Doctors hope she will be well enough to go home for Christmas, but they have warned that her recovery will be slow and that she might never be as active as before.
